main_finding: Defines concepts including measurand, measurement procedure, result, error, and uncertainty.
motionlab_relevance: Controls terminology and discourages calling an imperfect comparison method ground truth.
limitations: General guidance; does not prescribe a biomechanics protocol.

main_finding: Provides general rules for evaluating and expressing measurement uncertainty.
motionlab_relevance: Basis for the future uncertainty budget and explicit measurement model.
limitations: Requires justified inputs and assumptions; M2 has no numerical inputs.

main_finding: Provides a Monte Carlo method for propagating distributions through measurement models.
motionlab_relevance: Supports later nonlinear propagation after input distributions are justified.
limitations: Does not justify hypothetical distributions or turn sensitivity scenarios into empirical uncertainty.

main_finding: Correlation is misleading for agreement; differences and limits of agreement address a different question.
motionlab_relevance: Supports prioritizing signed differences and agreement over correlation.
limitations: Simple formulation assumes independent pairs and requires contextual acceptability criteria.

main_finding: Extends agreement analysis to repeated observations when the underlying quantity is fixed or changing.
motionlab_relevance: Frames and trials require hierarchical treatment rather than independent-pair formulas.
limitations: Exact model depends on the eventual sampling design and estimand.

population_or_scope: 53 studies of sports and functional tasks
main_finding: Reliability and validity vary across systems, tasks, planes, joints, and metrics; squat and landing reliability was often favorable.
motionlab_relevance: Supports task-specific validation and the narrow sagittal-knee scope.
limitations: High heterogeneity prevents transfer of pooled expectations to MotionLab.

main_finding: Several sagittal lower-limb measures showed moderate-to-high validity but performance varied and further validation was required.
motionlab_relevance: Reinforces plane- and task-specific evidence boundaries.
limitations: Focuses 3D systems and jump-landing rather than MotionLab's single-camera 2D squat.

main_finding: Reliability was often good while criterion validity ranged widely and was commonly poor or moderate.
motionlab_relevance: Shows why repeatability cannot substitute for agreement and why a 2D quantity must remain explicitly projected.
limitations: Running and mixed angle definitions are not the MotionLab squat protocol.

main_finding: Reliability and validity varied; setup, rater, plane, joint, and outcome definition affected results.
motionlab_relevance: Supports standardized setup and explicit reference-operator characterization.

method_or_reference: single camera with and without reflective markers
main_finding: Reliability depended on rater experience, joint, gait event, and marker condition.
motionlab_relevance: Supports testing marker visibility and intra/inter-rater reference repeatability.
limitations: Walking and GAITRite setup differ from a squat and do not establish accuracy.

method_or_reference: tablet app versus Vicon 3D motion analysis
main_finding: 2D test-retest reliability was high for knee measurement but systematic between-method differences remained and varied by joint.
motionlab_relevance: Directly supports separating reference repeatability from agreement in a squat task.
limitations: Different software, angle construction, 30 fps capture, and 2D-versus-3D measurands limit transfer.

method_or_reference: automated 2D marker tracking versus 3D motion capture
main_finding: Agreement depended on the outcome and participant despite useful low-cost sagittal measurements.
motionlab_relevance: Supports preserving full trajectories and validating each defined output rather than the pipeline generically.
limitations: Running at 120 Hz with visible markers is not the intended squat system.

method_or_reference: OpenPose angles versus marker-based motion capture
main_finding: Camera viewpoint materially affected joint-angle estimates and occlusion patterns.
motionlab_relevance: Supports treating camera pose as part of the instrument and controlling the baseline view.
limitations: Model, movement, views, and 2D/3D comparison differ from MotionLab; numerical effects are not transferable.
